outcomes.single: one dominant browser signal routes to one mode
outcomes.orderedBundle: multiple explicitly named browser tools route in tie-break order
outcomes.defer: unclear or generic browser phrasing asks for disambiguation

routerPolicy.defaultResourceContract: A scored route assembles exactly the selected mode's declared resources. defaultResource is consulted only when no mode scores, and then only as the defer-time suggestion offered alongside disambiguation. It is never added to a scored route's resource set.
routerPolicy.discoveryClassesContract: Classes listed here are hub discovery and defer evidence only. No mode's scoring classes reference them, so a prompt that matches only discovery vocabulary scores zero modes and takes the defer outcome instead of fanning out to every mode.

hub-identity.note: Discovery-only. Hub-level vocabulary that identifies this hub, not any one mode. Deliberately unreferenced by routerSignals, so hub-identity-only prompts defer.

generic-browser-automation.note: Discovery-only. Generic browser-automation phrasing names no tool, so it never scores a mode. A prompt that matches only these phrases defers. The Aside and Bladebro agentic phrasing lives here too, because a bare agentic request belongs to neither mode.

browser-debug.note: Debugging and inspection vocabulary. It stays here and out of the Bladebro classes, so a debugging request resolves to Chrome DevTools and never to Bladebro on its own.

aside-devtools-aliases.note: Bare aside is kept: without it, requests such as "run aside on the pricing page" or "open aside and log in" name the tool and still defer. Stage two only runs after the advisor picks this hub, so ordinary-prose uses of the word never reach it.

aside-repl-evidence.note: Deterministic REPL replay and evidence capture. These phrases carry no agentic or stealth qualifier, because agentic and stealth signed-in work belongs to the Bladebro classes.

bladebro-workflow.note: Agentic branching, stealth signed-in work and caller-owned browser attachment. Tie-break order places Chrome DevTools first on debugging overlap and Aside first on deterministic signed-in overlap.
